QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_15

question.text: 'Theory of Change' (ToC) in the context of Logic Model design MOST closely refers to:

answer.text: A government schedule of eligible CSR activities

An articulated causal chain from inputs through activities, outputs, outcomes to impact — with explicit assumptions at each link — that explains HOW and WHY the intervention is expected to produce the desired change

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes Theory of Change as a way to map how and why a desired change is expected to occur, with emphasis on assumptions and on a causal pathway running from activities through to impact. ToC is the narrative articulation of the logic that the Logical Framework formalises. The Trap: Donor-pledge templates, CSR schedules, and statutory audit programmes are thematic distractors that miss the causal-chain and assumption-mapping essence of Theory of Change. Note: When reading a ToC narrative, paying attention to phrases such as "will lead to" or "therefore" is a quick way to surface the underlying assumptions that should be stated explicitly in the logic model.
